description: Canonical interoperability contracts for A.R.I.A. entities. These contracts define identity, provenance, temporal semantics, confidence, probability, relationships, knowledge graph edges, and shared behavior across cognition, reasoning, knowledge, experience, and learning systems.

principles.canonical_identity: Every persisted first-class entity has one stable canonical identifier.
principles.typed_identity: Identifiers use a canonical entity prefix followed by a globally unique UUID.
principles.case_experience_separation: A diagnostic case represents an investigation or work episode. An experience record represents validated learning derived from one or more qualifying cases or observations. A case is not itself an experience record.
principles.observation_interpretation_separation: Observed information remains distinguishable from interpretation, inference, hypothesis, and conclusion.
principles.probability_confidence_separation: Probability represents estimated likelihood. Confidence represents trust in the quality or support of an estimate, observation, relationship, or conclusion.
principles.provenance_required: Technical information must retain sufficient provenance to explain where it came from and how it was transformed.
principles.relationship_explicitness: Semantic relationships are represented explicitly. Reverse relationships are never assumed unless explicitly defined.
principles.knowledge_reuse: Canonical technical concepts are created once and reused. Manufacturer-, product-, scope-, team-, and user-specific applicability is expressed through context, relationships, and experience overlays rather than duplicating canonical knowledge.
principles.validated_learning: Historical interactions do not automatically become learned experience. Learning eligibility requires sufficient validation under the Learning Engine.

base_entity_contract.description: Minimum shared contract for canonical persisted entities.

temporal_contract.description: Shared temporal semantics for entities whose truth, applicability, or validity can change over time.

valid_from.description: Beginning of the period during which the represented fact or relationship is considered applicable.

valid_to.description: End of the applicability period. Null means no known end.

observed_at.description: Time the underlying condition was actually observed.

recorded_at.description: Time the information was recorded by ARIA or another source.

confidence_contract.description: Confidence represents trust in the quality, support, or reliability of information. Confidence is not probability.

basis.description: Human-readable or machine-generated explanation of why this confidence value is appropriate.

probability_contract.description: Probability represents estimated likelihood of a hypothesis or mutually competing state within a defined reasoning context.

provenance_contract.description: Shared lineage contract for technical information.

relationship_contract.description: Canonical contract for a first-class semantic relationship between canonical entities. A relationship may be case-specific, evidentiary, experiential, operational, or broadly semantic. Relationship records are distinct from persisted knowledge graph edges.
rules: A reverse relationship must not be inferred solely because a forward relationship exists.
Relationship direction and semantics are determined by the canonical relationship type definition.
Relationship confidence describes trust in the asserted relationship and does not represent hypothesis probability.
Relationships may connect evidence, hypotheses, actions, cases, experiences, users, technical entities, sources, and other canonical entities.
Case-specific support and contradiction semantics should be represented by relationship records when relationship strength, provenance, temporal applicability, or auditability is material.

knowledge_node_contract.description: Canonical node persisted in the reusable technical knowledge graph.

canonical_entity_id.description: Canonical technical concept represented by this graph node.

knowledge_edge_contract.description: Persisted edge within ARIA's reusable technical knowledge graph. A knowledge edge is distinct from a general relationship record. Knowledge edges represent graph structure and reusable technical knowledge rather than transient case-specific reasoning state.

source_entity_id.description: Optional denormalized reference to the canonical entity represented by the source node.

target_entity_id.description: Optional denormalized reference to the canonical entity represented by the target node.

rules: Knowledge graph edges represent reusable technical knowledge and graph topology.
A knowledge edge does not automatically create a case-specific relationship record.
A case-specific relationship may reference or be informed by knowledge graph information without duplicating the underlying canonical technical entities.
User-specific experience must not require duplication of the canonical knowledge graph.

case_contract.description: A diagnostic or operational investigation. A case is not an Experience Ledger record.
rules: Cases may contain or reference evidence, hypotheses, actions, events, context, outcomes, and reasoning history.
An unresolved or unvalidated case must not automatically influence validated experience statistics.
One or more Experience Ledger records may later be derived from a qualifying case.

evidence_contract.description: Observed, measured, supplied, recorded, or derived information used during reasoning.
rules: Observation must remain distinguishable from interpretation.
Derived evidence retains lineage to its parent evidence.
Multiple representations of the same underlying source must not automatically be treated as independent confirmation.
Evidence reliability and hypothesis probability are separate concepts.

hypothesis_contract.description: Case-specific candidate explanation evaluated by ARIA.
rules: A hypothesis instance is distinct from the canonical technical entity it evaluates.
Historical priors are not current-case evidence.
Probability changes must remain auditable.
Confidence in a probability estimate remains distinct from the probability value.
Requirements for evidence that does not yet exist must not be represented as evidence IDs.

action_contract.description: A diagnostic, verification, corrective, operational, or information-gathering action.

experience_contract.description: Validated historical learning derived from qualifying cases, outcomes, actions, and observations. Experience is distinct from the diagnostic case that produced it.
rules: Experience must be derived only from sufficiently validated information.
User-specific experience references canonical technical entities rather than duplicating them.
Experience may influence priors and decision strategy but does not alter canonical technical truth.
Experience statistics must preserve the context under which the experience was observed.

user_experience_overlay_contract.description: User-specific historical overlay used to personalize ARIA's priors and diagnostic strategy without duplicating canonical technical knowledge.
rules: User-specific statistics must be computed from validated experience appropriate to the active context.
Insufficient user-specific sample size should cause progressive widening to team, product, manufacturer, scope, or domain experience as defined by the Probability Engine.
User history must not be represented as an intrinsic property of the technical entity.
ARIA must preserve the distinction between a user's historical tendency and the evidence present in the current case.

interoperability_rules.rule: A diagnostic case uses the case_ prefix and must not use the exp_ prefix.
An Experience Ledger record uses the exp_ prefix and must remain independently addressable from its source case.
Evidence uses the evd_ prefix and must retain provenance.
Hypotheses use the hyp_ prefix and are case-specific instances evaluating canonical technical entities.
General semantic relationships use the rel_ prefix.
Persisted reusable knowledge graph edges use the ke_ prefix and are distinct from general rel_ relationship records.
Canonical technical concepts are not duplicated merely to express manufacturer, scope, team, user, or case applicability.
Confidence and probability must not be treated as interchangeable values.
A reverse semantic relationship is not implied unless explicitly defined by the relationship registry or represented as a separate relationship.
Historical experience may influence diagnostic priors but must not override contradictory direct evidence from the active case.
Unvalidated cases must not automatically contribute to validated user, team, product, manufacturer, or domain experience statistics.
